domains.title: Plan supply chain & network
domains.short: Balance demand, supply, capacity, inventory and network policy.
domains.scope: Demand/supply/capacity planning, inventory and deployment policy, logistics network design, service policy and performance targets.
apqc: 4.1 Plan for and align supply chain resources
domains.boundary: Planning ↔ order, source, transform, warehouse and transport execution
questions: Where is the first plan-to-execution state divergence detected?
Which constraint is modeled late or outside the system of record?
Which service/cost trade-off is approved without quantified impact?
How quickly does execution evidence trigger replanning?

domains.title: Customer, commercial & order
domains.short: Shape the offer; quote, validate and manage the order commitment.
domains.scope: Customer enquiry, solution/rate design, quote and terms, order capture, validation, promise, amendment and cancellation. Quote and order remain separate underlying processes.
apqc: Sales bid / proposal / quote processes (separate mapping)
questions: Are quote, booking/order and operational instruction represented as distinct objects?
Where do rate/terms diverge from the executed service?
Which validation is duplicated across channels or actors?
What change is accepted without propagating to downstream commitments?

domains.title: Source & procure
domains.short: Govern sourcing, select providers, and establish and manage supply commitments.
domains.scope: Sourcing governance, category planning, supplier/provider selection, contracts, requisition and purchase order, direct/indirect procurement, supplier management and source returns.
domains.boundary: Business need ↔ supplier/provider commitment ↔ receipt and payment
questions: Where is a provider selected without a current capability or compliance view?
Which contract or tariff term is not machine-readable downstream?
What commitment exists outside the purchase/booking object?
Which supplier event fails to update the inbound plan?

domains.title: Transform, manufacture & value-add
domains.short: Convert material, asset or service inputs into the promised output.
domains.scope: Product manufacture, service transformation, maintenance/repair/overhaul and logistics value-added services, including scheduling, issue, execute, inspect/test, pack and release.
domains.boundary: Released order and inputs ↔ controlled transformation ↔ available output
questions: Which execution state is reported only after completion?
Where does quality evidence fail to block release?
What material genealogy or service proof cannot be reconstructed?
Which rework loop is hidden from cost and capacity planning?

domains.title: Inventory & warehousing
domains.short: Receive, store, control, pick, pack, stage and transfer inventory.
domains.scope: Inbound receiving/unloading/inspection, putaway, storage, slotting, replenishment, picking, packing, staging, loading, cross-dock, counting/adjustment, VAS and yard/dock work.
domains.boundary: External arrival ↔ node custody and inventory ↔ transport handoff
questions: Where does physical inventory diverge from the digital state?
Which handoff lacks unit/location/time evidence?
What queue or dwell time is invisible to upstream and downstream plans?
Which exception is resolved locally but not reflected in the system of record?

domains.title: Transportation & distribution
domains.short: Plan, buy, tender/book, execute and monitor movement across nodes and legs.
domains.scope: Transport request, mode/service selection, rating, routing, consolidation, capacity procurement, tender/booking, appointment/equipment, pickup, origin handling, carriage, transshipment, visibility and freight-settlement handoffs. Transportation terminates at the handoff into destination/last-mile execution.
domains.boundary: Shipment demand ↔ contracted capacity ↔ physical leg and node events ↔ destination/last-mile handoff
questions: At which node or leg does responsibility change without a shared event?
Where are capacity and commercial commitments represented differently?
Which exception is detected after its recovery window closes?
What executed charge lacks a traceable service/evidence basis?

domains.title: Trade, customs & regulatory
domains.short: Classify, screen, declare, assess, inspect and release cross-border movement.
domains.scope: Classification, origin, valuation, licensing, restricted-party/sanctions controls, security filings, export/import declarations, duties/taxes, broker management, inspection/hold/release and post-entry activity.
apqc: Cross-enterprise risk/compliance processes; no forced subordinate mapping
domains.boundary: Commercial and transport data ↔ authority/broker ↔ border release
questions: Which declaration field is re-keyed from an existing authoritative object?
Where is regulatory applicability decided without an auditable rule/version?
Which upstream change fails to invalidate a filing or license check?
How is hold/release state propagated to every execution actor?

domains.title: Delivery & last mile
domains.short: Plan destination execution, deliver or install, and capture acceptance evidence.
domains.scope: Destination readiness, appointment, last-mile dispatch, delivery or installation, delivery attempt, POD/acceptance and failed-delivery handoff. Customer interaction is mapped separately under Customer Service & Operations.
scor: F1–F3 delivery, installation and acceptance elements
domains.boundary: Destination handoff ↔ recipient/installation action ↔ acceptance or failed-delivery recovery
questions: What proves delivery to the correct party, place, time and condition?
Which failure reason and evidence trigger the correct operational recovery?
Where does delivery status differ across carrier, TMS and recipient channels?
Which delivery completion fails to trigger the required downstream state?

domains.title: Returns, reverse & recovery
domains.short: Authorize, collect, receive, diagnose, disposition and financially adjust returns.
domains.scope: Return initiation/authorization, reverse transport, receiving, diagnosis/test, repair/refurbish, disposition, storage, document update, replacement and financial/contract adjustment.
domains.boundary: Customer/supplier return signal ↔ reverse custody ↔ disposition and settlement
questions: Can the return be linked to original commercial, physical and financial records?
Where is disposition decided without condition/value evidence?
Which reverse movement lacks visibility or capacity planning?
What financial adjustment is delayed by missing operational proof?

domains.title: Finance, billing & settlement
domains.short: Run distinct revenue, payable and freight-settlement cycles.
domains.scope: Customer billing/AR/collections and adjustments; supplier/carrier invoice audit/AP/payment; freight accrual, rating, allocation and settlement; trade-finance touchpoints where applicable.
scor: Commercial/fulfil/return financial touchpoints; not treated as one SCOR hierarchy
apqc: 9.6 Process accounts payable and expense reimbursements
domains.boundary: Operational evidence and commercial terms ↔ financial subledger ↔ bank/party
questions: Which operational completion fails to trigger billing or accrual?
Can every charge be traced to contract, rate, event and evidence?
Where are P2P, O2C and freight settlement incorrectly collapsed?
Which dispute category masks a master-data or execution defect?

domains.title: Execution control & exception recovery
domains.short: Observe, detect, recover, escalate and learn across every execution domain.
domains.scope: A cross-domain control rail for expected/actual state comparison, severity, ownership, response clock, containment, recovery, communication, escalation, closure and root-cause feedback.
scor: Exception handling within the applicable execution process
apqc: Cross-enterprise performance, risk and process-management crosswalks; not APQC 6.0 Customer Service
domains.boundary: Observed variance ↔ accountable recovery ↔ corrected execution state or plan
questions: Which critical variance has no event, owner or response clock?
Where does an alert exist without a recoverable action?
What exception is closed without correcting the authoritative state?
Which recurring root cause is invisible because cases use inconsistent classifications?

domains.title: Resolution, claims & disputes
domains.short: Route cargo/service claims, billing disputes and insurance recovery through distinct controls.
domains.scope: A Universe umbrella with separate branches for cargo/service claims, billing/commercial disputes and insurance recovery/subrogation. Each branch uses different standing, evidence, liability, approval and settlement rules.
sub: Cargo/service claim: notice → evidence → liability → loss → adjudication
Billing/commercial dispute: charge → contract/rate → invoice → evidence → adjustment
Insurance recovery/subrogation: insured event → policy → coverage → recovery
scor: Return/service-recovery touchpoints; not a SCOR primary process
apqc: Finance, customer-service and legal/process crosswalks; no single APQC claim hierarchy asserted
domains.boundary: Operational/commercial evidence ↔ applicable contract/convention/policy ↔ financial resolution
questions: Is the applicable contract, carriage regime, policy and time bar explicit?
Which evidence is collected only after it becomes unavailable?
Are cargo claims, billing disputes and insurance recoveries routed through different rules?
Can recurrence be traced to the responsible process and control?

domains.title: Customer service & operations
domains.short: Manage enquiries, notifications, service requests, complaints and case resolution.
domains.scope: Customer contact and service operations linked to—rather than substituted for—authoritative order, shipment, delivery, billing and claim states.
scor: Customer contact touchpoints across Order, Fulfill and Return; not a SCOR primary process
domains.boundary: Customer contact ↔ authoritative operational/financial state ↔ accountable response or action
questions: Which customer contact exists because an operational event is missing or late?
Can the case link to the authoritative order, shipment, invoice or claim?
Where does the contact channel promise an action it cannot control?
Which closure code hides an unresolved execution state?

domains.title: Assets, equipment & maintenance
domains.short: Plan, allocate, inspect, maintain and reposition operating assets and equipment.
domains.scope: Fleet, vehicle, trailer, container, ULD, wagon/railcar, material-handling equipment and facility-asset availability, allocation, inspection, maintenance, utilization and repositioning—conditional by operating model.
scor: T3 Transform Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul
apqc: Selected asset-management and transportation-fleet crosswalks; not represented as SCOR hierarchy
domains.boundary: Asset ownership/control ↔ availability and assignment ↔ safe execution and maintenance evidence
questions: Which equipment shortage is discovered after the service commitment?
Can condition, custody, availability and maintenance status be reconciled?
Where is empty-equipment repositioning invisible to network planning?
Which operating role owns versus controls versus uses the asset?

domains.title: Master & reference data
domains.short: Govern party, location, item, asset, code and relationship identities across systems.
domains.scope: Cross-enterprise identity, reference-data, code-set, hierarchy, relationship, quality, stewardship, version and distribution controls. No universal shipment identifier is assumed.
apqc: Enterprise information/data-management crosswalks; detailed APQC nodes not reconstructed here
domains.boundary: Issuing authority/source system ↔ governed identity and relationships ↔ consuming systems
questions: Which object has no named authoritative source by scope?
Where do party, place, item, equipment or shipment keys diverge?
Can identifiers be related without claiming one universal ID?
Which regulatory or commercial process uses an obsolete code/version?

enterpriseCoverage.gap: Freeze sector- and jurisdiction-specific sourcing controls before execution modelling.

enterpriseCoverage.gap: Tolerance, tax and approval rules require A3–A5 configuration.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Order-to-Cash

enterpriseCoverage.gap: Revenue-recognition policy and channel variants require implementation evidence.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Contract lifecycle management
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Authoring, negotiation, approval, obligation execution, change, renewal and closure.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Sector clauses, legal review and obligation semantics need execution research.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Pricing, rating and commercial management
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Product/service pricing, transport rating, surcharge logic, quote governance and executed-charge traceability.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: No source-native pricing/rating hierarchy is claimed; tariffs, rating logic, decisions, controls and approval tolerances require a named A3–A5 source pack.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Master data management
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Authority, identity, quality, hierarchy, relationship, version and distribution for core business objects.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Object-level authority must be assigned per enterprise scope.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Supplier lifecycle and performance
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Onboard, qualify, segment, collaborate, monitor, remediate and exit suppliers/providers.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Qualification evidence and scorecard definitions remain organization-specific.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Inventory optimization
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Multi-echelon policy, safety stock, service segmentation, replenishment and obsolescence trade-offs.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: SCOR/APQC anchor planning and inventory work, but no source-native optimization taxonomy is asserted; method, segmentation, parameters and decision ownership require A3–A5 evidence.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Manufacturing
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Plan, schedule, execute, inspect, release and reconcile product, service and MRO transformation.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Industry process parameters and control-system detail require a named implementation profile.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Product and item lifecycle
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Concept, definition, introduction, change, publication, traceability and retirement of products/items.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Engineering-change and regulatory-product detail needs sector research.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Quality management
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Quality planning, inspection, nonconformance, corrective action, release and continual improvement.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Sector-specific quality standards and sampling plans remain conditional.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Customer service
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Authenticate, classify, answer, coordinate, resolve, communicate and learn from customer contacts.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Channel, entitlement and SLA rules require implementation detail.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Claims, disputes and deductions
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Cargo/service claims, billing disputes, deductions and insurance recovery remain separate branches.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Standing, liability, policy, time bars and deduction rules must be resolved by case.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Revenue assurance
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Protect completeness, accuracy and timeliness from service commitment through charge, invoice, collection and adjustment.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Revenue assurance remains an analytical/control construct, not a source-native process hierarchy; revenue rules, leakage tests and accounting policy require enterprise evidence.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Network design and capacity
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Nodes, lanes, partners, capacity, service and cost scenarios across strategic and tactical horizons.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: SCOR anchors network design, but scenario-state transitions, decision rights, capacity controls, data granularity and approval evidence require implementation design.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Carrier and provider management
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Source, contract, onboard, allocate, monitor and remediate transport and logistics providers.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Mode, lane and provider qualification rules must be frozen at A3–A5.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Warehouse and fulfilment
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Receive, store, control, pick, pack, stage, load and evidence node execution.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Facility-specific tasks, automation and labour rules require A3–A5 decomposition.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Returns and reverse logistics
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Authorize, move, receive, diagnose, disposition, recover value and financially adjust returns.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Entitlement, grading and disposition economics require execution detail.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Global trade management
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Classify, screen, license, declare, assess, hold/release and retain cross-border evidence.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Jurisdiction, goods, parties, procedure and effective instruments must be resolved per execution case.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Risk and resilience
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Identify exposure, monitor signals, model scenarios, respond, continue and learn across the network.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Threat models, tolerances and continuity strategies remain enterprise-specific.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Assets, fleet and equipment
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Plan, acquire, maintain, certify, allocate, operate, inspect and retire physical assets.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Mode-specific maintenance, certification and inspection rules remain conditional.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Workforce and labour management
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Workforce demand, skill, qualification, shift, safety, productivity and contingent-labour controls.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: APQC 7.0 provides an enterprise category and ISO 30414 supports reporting evidence; neither is a supply-chain workforce process taxonomy. Labour, qualification, collective and local safety sources require targeted research.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Financial supply chain
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Working capital, trade finance, receivables, payables, cash, guarantees and settlement linked to operational evidence.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Financing products, bank rules and accounting policies require implementation research.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Sustainability, ESG and carbon
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Activity data, organizational and value-chain emissions, transport-chain calculations, targets and evidence.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Boundaries, factors, assurance and regulatory disclosure regimes require explicit profiles.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Governance, controls and compliance
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Policy, obligation, control, evidence, monitoring, remediation and assurance across enterprise processes.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: Control owners, test plans and jurisdictional obligations require enterprise configuration.

enterpriseCoverage.name: Knowledge and decision management
enterpriseCoverage.provenance: SOURCE-NATIVE CATEGORY + MANAGEMENT-SYSTEM / NOTATION STARTING POINT
enterpriseCoverage.scope: Decision rights, knowledge capture, reuse, lineage, learning and human/automated decision evidence.
enterpriseCoverage.gap: ISO 30401 supports a knowledge-management system and DMN 1.5 supports decision notation; neither supplies an end-to-end supply-chain knowledge/decision taxonomy. Domain-specific decision and evidence sources remain required.

modes.name: No execution overlay
modes.desc: Use mode-neutral shipment, service request, booking, equipment, event and transport-document concepts.
modes.core: UN/CEFACT reference data models · GS1 within published scope
modes.applicability: No mode-specific or jurisdiction-specific standard is loaded.
modes.objects: Shipment · transport service request · booking · node · leg · equipment · event

modes.name: Ocean container · FCL
modes.desc: Container-shipping reference is resolved across three parallel source-native journeys: Shipment (booking through payment/documentation), Equipment (container pickup through return) and Vessel (departure, port calls and arrival).
modes.core: DCSA Industry Blueprint 2026.Q1 + current DCSA standards · IMO operational/safety/data-harmonization instruments · SMDG/TIC4.0 where adopted
modes.applicability: DCSA applies to container-shipping interfaces and non-competitive reference processes; liability, customs, terminal, flag/port and national rules depend on contract, lane, role and jurisdiction.
modes.objects: Container · seal · ocean booking · shipping instructions · B/L/sea waybill · VGM · port call

modes.name: Ocean · LCL / consolidation
modes.desc: LCL remains a distinct execution model: consolidation/deconsolidation, CFS handling, contracting-carrier/forwarder layers and House↔Master document relationships sit around the container-carrier interface.
modes.core: FIATA instruments and eFBL data standard · UN/CEFACT MMT RDM · DCSA at the applicable container-carrier interface · customs/terminal sources by context
modes.applicability: No universal LCL/CFS sequence is inferred. House/master relationships, contracting role, liability and local CFS/customs handling must resolve from the service contract, sources and jurisdiction.
modes.objects: House B/L · master B/L · consolidation · container · CFS handoff · deconsolidation

modes.name: Air cargo
modes.desc: Air booking, AWB/e-AWB, cargo acceptance, handling, ULD, security and dangerous-goods execution.
modes.core: IATA ONE Record/Cargo-XML/e-AWB · ICAO safety/security instruments
modes.applicability: Air booking/capacity reservation is distinct from the AWB/e-AWB transport document and evidence of the contract of carriage. Montreal Convention 1999 is not assumed; contract, international-carriage conditions and state-party scope must resolve first.
modes.objects: Air booking · AWB/e-AWB · piece · ULD · acceptance · flight movement · security status

modes.name: Road · FTL / truckload
modes.desc: Load tender, acceptance, appointment, dispatch, driver/vehicle, pickup, linehaul and delivery.
modes.core: UN/CEFACT MMT semantics · GS1 where adopted
modes.applicability: CMR/e-CMR and North-American X12/FMCSA packs are alternatives selected by lane and jurisdiction—not one combined regime.
modes.objects: Load tender · tender response · vehicle · trailer · driver · CMR note or BOL/eBOL · POD

modes.name: Road · LTL / groupage
modes.desc: Classification/rating, pickup, terminal cross-dock, linehaul, interchange and destination delivery.
modes.core: UN/CEFACT MMT semantics · GS1 where adopted
modes.applicability: NMFC, SCAC, SPLC and X12 are North-American overlays; they are not global LTL standards.
modes.objects: LTL shipment · handling unit · terminal · network reference/pro number · eBOL/consignment note

modes.name: Rail Freight
modes.desc: Rail booking, consignment, wagon/container interchange, train movement and terminal events.
modes.core: UN/CEFACT MMT RDM · UIC/RailData where adopted
modes.applicability: CIM/COTIF, OSJD/SMGS, EU interoperability and North-American AAR/X12 packs are selected by contract, route and network.
modes.objects: Rail booking · CIM/SMGS consignment note · wagon/railcar · train · intermodal unit · terminal event

modes.name: Postal network
modes.desc: Postal item acceptance, receptacle/dispatch exchange, postal EDI, customs item data and delivery events.
modes.core: UPU postal standards and postal-supply-chain semantics
modes.applicability: UPU sources govern the postal network and designated-operator exchanges; they are not automatically private CEP standards.
modes.objects: Postal item · S10 identifier · receptacle · dispatch · ITMATT/customs item data · postal event

modes.name: Private CEP / express parcel
modes.desc: Private-network induction, sort, linehaul, customs where applicable, delivery attempt and recipient event.
modes.core: UN/CEFACT/GS1 semantics where adopted · private-network operating model
modes.applicability: Private CEP networks are modelled separately from the UPU designated postal network.
modes.objects: Parcel item · package identifier · bag/container · sort event · route/stop · delivery attempt · POD

modes.name: Inland waterway / barge
modes.desc: Barge/vessel booking, contract of carriage, terminal handoff, inland navigation, port/river events and delivery.
modes.core: UN/CEFACT MMT RDM · Atlas generic inland-waterway execution shell
modes.applicability: CMNI is not assumed; apply it only when its carriage scope resolves. CCNR and CESNI likewise apply only within their navigation, technical and information scopes. Corridor, vessel, goods and national law determine the operative pack.
modes.objects: Barge/vessel booking · consignment · vessel/barge · terminal handoff · navigation event · inland-waterway transport document

modes.name: Pipeline transport
modes.desc: Nomination, scheduling, allocation, measurement, quality, custody transfer and imbalance/settlement.
modes.core: Atlas conceptual process shell · UN/CEFACT commercial semantics where applicable
modes.applicability: Universe provides conceptual coverage only; the authoritative pack must be frozen by commodity and regulator before L3–L5 modelling.
modes.objects: Nomination · batch/flow schedule · meter point · quality certificate · custody-transfer record · imbalance

modes.name: Warehouse / fulfilment node
modes.desc: Receiving, storage, inventory, picking, packing, staging, loading, cross-dock, yard and returns execution.
modes.core: APQC 4.4.3 · SCOR Fulfill/Return mappings · GS1 EPCIS · ISA-95 where applicable
modes.applicability: Node type, commodity, automation, bonded status and national safety/regulatory scope determine the controls.
modes.objects: Handling unit · location · stock state · wave · task · receipt · shipment readiness

modes.name: Intermodal / Multimodal service chain
modes.desc: Customer solution, capacity procurement, house documents, agent handoffs, mode changes and end-to-end settlement. Freight forwarder remains an operating role.
modes.core: FIATA instruments/practice · UN/CEFACT MMT RDM · mode-specific child standards
modes.applicability: Each leg retains its own carrier, contract, document, liability and jurisdiction even when the service is sold end-to-end.
modes.objects: House transport document · master document · service chain · leg · agent instruction · handoff event

modes.name: Last mile
modes.desc: Recipient requirements, dispatch, route, delivery attempt, evidence and failed-delivery recovery.
modes.applicability: Postal and private CEP last mile remain distinct; service, recipient, goods and local law determine the process.
modes.objects: Delivery order · stop · route · recipient instruction · delivery attempt · POD · failed-delivery case
